quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 40 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders.
Turn just your head.
Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Turn just your head to look through a turn. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the animal loses interest.
Slow down, let the dog get close, then quickly speed up and leave.
Swerve around the animal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, let the dog get close, then quickly speed up and leave.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, slow down and downshift. As the dog gets close, quickly accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: When carrying a load, it should be:

options.text: Secured as high as possible.
Secured as low as possible.
Secured on a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Secure loads as low as possible. This keeps the motorcycle balanced and stable.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Swerve around the dog.
Slow down, let the dog approach, and speed up away from it.
Park and wait for the dog to lose interest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, let the dog approach, and speed up away from it.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. Downshift and slow down to let the dog get close. Then accelerate quickly to leave it behind.

questions.question: When being passed, where should a motorcyclist ride in the lane?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding too close to the passing driver creates a dangerous situation for both of you.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked. You can usually control the motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, you should:

options.text: Hold the handgrips firmly and stay off the brakes.
Shift your weight toward the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel and pull off the road immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly and stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly and go straight. Only brake if you know which tire is flat. Leave the road slowly after the motorcycle has slowed down.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear brake on good pavement, you should:

options.text: Let go of the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If the rear tire locks on good pavement, leave it locked until you stop completely. You can control the motorcycle with a locked rear wheel if the road has good traction and the motorcycle stays upright and straight.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, how does a motorcycle respond to turning?

options.text: More slowly than usual.
More quickly than usual.
Normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to the motorcycle. With more weight, the motorcycle responds more slowly to turns, speed changes, and other movements.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, there is usually an oily strip. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
Not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease buildup. The oily strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can often stay to the side and avoid it while still riding in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the rear brake first.
Apply the front brake first.
Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using only the rear brake may prevent you from learning how to use the front brake properly when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: The best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle is to:

options.text: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
Avoid busy traffic areas.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Watch the road far ahead of you to spot dangers early. This gives you time to react and avoid problems before they happen.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they can make vehicles behind you look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, who should yield?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: A person is considered legally intoxicated at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent
0.12 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Driving any vehicle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, it should have all of these qualities, except:

options.text: Meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
Fits snugly.
Has no defects.
Looks attractive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Looks attractive.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards, fits snugly, and has no damage such as cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance does not matter for safety.

questions.question: For motorcycle riders, eye protection is:

options.text: Required.
Recommended but not required.
Not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders must use proper eye protection when riding in Georgia.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you on the left, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the right side can tempt the passing driver to cut back into your lane too quickly.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of your lane should you be in?

options.text: Right
Center
Left

questions.correctAnswerText: Left
questions.explanation: Stay in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass another vehicle on the left.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle ahead so you can use its lights to see the road.
Keep riding at your normal speed to avoid being hit from behind.
Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, slow down and increase your following distance. You cannot see as far, so you need more time and space to react to hazards.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while stopping, you should:

options.text: Keep applying the front brake.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks during a hard stop, release the front brake immediately and then apply it firmly again. Use both brakes together when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and slow down by easing off the throttle. Apply the brake of the tire that is still good, and carefully steer toward the side of the road as you slow down.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn your head only, not your shoulders, to look through the turn.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head only, not your shoulders, to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head and keep your eyes level. Turning your shoulders can cause you to steer off course.

questions.question: If passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may go faster than the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You may pass in a no passing zone if you started the pass in a passing zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be done at or below the posted speed limit and only where passing is allowed.

questions.question: The key to making a quick turn is to:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Lean your motorcycle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean your motorcycle quickly.
questions.explanation: To make a sharp turn, lean your motorcycle quickly in the direction you want to turn. The sharper the turn, the more you must lean.

questions.question: When positioning your body on the motorcycle:

options.text: You should use your arms to hold yourself up.
Your arms should be used to steer the motorcycle.
You should have to stretch to reach the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your arms should be used to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Sit so your elbows are slightly bent when you hold the handlebars.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns of a divided roadway ahead.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Need less room to stop than larger vehicles.
Need as much room to stop as larger vehicles.
Can stop instantly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need as much room to stop as larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle based on road conditions. Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean do not pass. Dashed white lines mean you may pass if it is safe.

questions.question: During normal turns:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean in the same direction.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should not lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean in the same direction.
questions.explanation: In a normal turn, lean the motorcycle and your body together at the same angle. In a slow, tight turn, the motorcycle leans while you keep your body more upright.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move into the part of your lane that lets other drivers see you as early as possible.
Stop at the stop sign or signal and then proceed normally.
Flash your lights and sound your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the part of your lane that lets other drivers see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position yourself so other drivers can see you as soon as possible.

questions.question: When riding in a group on a straight road, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride in a single-file line.
Pair up.
Stagger their formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stagger their formation.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation keeps the group close while giving each rider enough space. Switch to single-file when turning, curving, or entering or leaving the road.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: Someone is following you too closely.
You will be slowing down suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be slowing down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are not as bright as car brake lights. Flash your brake light when slowing or stopping so others notice you are slowing down. This is especially important when slowing faster than expected.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Increase your following distance.
Decrease your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in one part of the lane and never change position.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Only ride in the center of the lane so others can see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position as conditions change to stay safe.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far side of your lane:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.
Has no effect on safety either way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far side of your lane when being passed. This may signal the other driver to move back into your lane before it is safe.
